domains.title: Agentic Architecture & Orchestration
domains.summary: How you build the agentic loop, how a coordinator controls subagents, how you enforce rules with code, and how you save and resume work. Largest domain.

taskStatements.title: Agentic Loops
taskStatements.oneLine: Loop on stop_reason. Stop on end_turn.
concept: An agentic loop is a cycle: send a request, Claude answers, if Claude wants a tool your code runs it and sends the result back, repeat until Claude is done.
The only reliable signal to control the loop is stop_reason. 'tool_use' = run the tool and continue. 'end_turn' = Claude is finished, stop.
Claude decides which tool to call next (model-driven). Your code does not pre-script the order of tool calls.
steps: Send the request with the messages array and the tools list.
Read the response and check stop_reason.
If 'tool_use': find each tool_use block and run each tool in your code.
Append the assistant message plus a user message with tool_result blocks (matching tool_use_id) to the conversation history.
Send the full history again and go back to step 2.
If 'end_turn': return the final text and exit the loop.

table.title: stop_reason values
rows: Claude asks for one or more tools
Run every tool_use block, send back a tool_result for each tool_use_id, continue
Output hit the token limit; answer is cut off
Do not treat as complete. Raise max_tokens or ask Claude to continue
A custom stop sequence was produced
A long server-side tool turn was paused
Send the response back as-is so Claude can continue
Terminate; route to fallback or human

taskStatements.examTip: Correct loop control = check stop_reason. Wrong: parse Claude's text for 'I am done'; stop when the reply has text content; use an iteration cap as the PRIMARY stop. A cap is only a safety net.
taskStatements.diagram: send request -> Claude responds -> check stop_reason -> (tool_use) run tools -> append tool_result -> loop again | (end_turn) return final answer

taskStatements.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
concept: One coordinator agent is the hub; specialized subagents (search, analysis, synthesis, report) are the spokes.
Subagents have isolated context: they do NOT inherit the coordinator's conversation history.
ALL communication goes through the coordinator. Subagents never talk to each other.
The coordinator decomposes the task, selects subagents dynamically, collects results, synthesizes, and handles errors.
steps: Read the request. Identify ALL sub-topics it covers.
Decompose into subtasks. Check the scope is complete (not too narrow).
Delegate each subtask to the right subagent with full context in the prompt.
Collect structured results.
Evaluate the synthesis for gaps. If gaps exist, re-delegate with targeted queries (iterative refinement).
Produce the final output.
taskStatements.examTip: Classic failure: the final report misses topics. Root cause = the coordinator's decomposition was too narrow (e.g. 'AI in creative industries' split into visual-art topics only). Fix the coordinator, not the search subagent.

taskStatements.title: Subagent Invocation and Context Passing
taskStatements.oneLine: Task tool. Pass context explicitly. Parallel = many Task calls in one response.
concept: The coordinator spawns a subagent with the Task tool. The coordinator's allowedTools MUST include 'Task' or it cannot spawn subagents.
Each subagent is defined by an AgentDefinition: a description (when to use it), a system prompt, and tool restrictions.
A subagent knows ONLY what you put in its prompt. Pass the previous findings, goal, constraints and output format explicitly.
steps: Add 'Task' to the coordinator's allowedTools.
Write an AgentDefinition for each subagent type (description, system prompt, allowed tools).
In the Task prompt include the complete findings from earlier steps (e.g. search results for the synthesis agent).
Keep content separate from metadata (source URL, document name, page number) so sources are not lost.
State the goal and quality criteria, not rigid step-by-step procedures.
For parallel work, emit multiple Task tool calls in ONE response. Do not spawn them one per turn.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Subagents run one after another and it is slow' -> several Task calls in a single coordinator response. 'Synthesis agent lacks information' -> pass prior results in the prompt (subagents do not share memory).

taskStatements.title: Workflow Enforcement and Handoff
taskStatements.oneLine: Programmatic gates for critical steps. Structured handoff to humans.
concept: Prompt-based guidance is probabilistic: works most of the time but has a non-zero failure rate. When a step MUST happen (e.g. verify identity before a refund) use programmatic enforcement.
A prerequisite gate is code that blocks a tool until a required earlier step has succeeded.
Multi-concern request (e.g. billing + shipping in one message): decompose into separate concerns, investigate each (in parallel, shared context), then give ONE unified answer.
steps: Identify the critical order (get_customer -> lookup_order -> process_refund).
Store the result of the first step in state (e.g. verified_customer_id).
Before the downstream tool runs, check the state in code.
If the check fails, block the call and return a clear error to Claude.
If it passes, allow the call.
Handoff to a human: write a structured summary (human has NO transcript) with customer ID, root cause, amounts, what was tried, recommended action.
taskStatements.examTip: Words like 'must always', 'compliance', 'financial', '12% of cases skip verification' -> programmatic enforcement (gate or hook), NOT a stronger prompt or more few-shot examples.

taskStatements.title: Agent SDK Hooks
concept: A hook is your code that runs at a fixed point in the agent loop. Hooks give deterministic guarantees; prompts only give probabilistic compliance.

table.title: Hook types
rows: Block policy violations (refund > $500), redirect to human escalation, validate arguments
After a tool runs, before Claude sees the result
Transform results: normalize dates (Unix -> ISO 8601), map status codes to words, trim fields

steps: Enforce a refund limit: register a PreToolUse hook for process_refund.
In the hook read the amount argument.
If amount > 500: deny the call and return 'Escalate to a human agent.'
If amount <= 500: allow the call.

Normalize mixed formats: register a PostToolUse hook on the tools that return mixed formats, convert timestamps to ISO 8601, convert codes to readable values, remove unneeded fields, return the clean result.
taskStatements.examTip: Different tools return dates in different formats and Claude makes errors -> PostToolUse normalization. Business rule must never be broken -> PreToolUse block.

taskStatements.title: Task Decomposition Strategies
taskStatements.oneLine: Prompt chaining for fixed steps. Dynamic decomposition for open tasks.
concept: Prompt chaining = fixed sequential pipeline; use when steps are known and predictable (code review: each file, then one integration pass).
Dynamic adaptive decomposition = plan changes with findings; use for open-ended tasks ('add tests to legacy codebase': map structure, find high-impact areas, adapt).
Attention dilution: when one pass reviews many files at once, quality drops - some files get deep feedback, others shallow, bugs are missed, findings contradict.
steps: Review a 14-file PR: split the PR into files.
Run a per-file local analysis pass on each file (local bugs, logic).
Run a separate cross-file integration pass (data flow, interfaces).
Merge and de-duplicate findings.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Inconsistent review depth across many files' -> per-file passes + integration pass. A bigger context window or bigger model is NOT the fix.

taskStatements.title: Session State and Resumption
concept: Choose how to continue prior work based on whether old tool results are still valid.

table.title: Resume vs fork vs new
rows: Continues a named session with full history
Prior context still valid. Tell Claude which files changed.
Creates a branch from a shared baseline
Compare two approaches from the same starting point
Starts clean; you inject a summary of key findings
Old tool results are stale (code changed a lot) or context is degraded

steps: Check if the earlier tool results are still true.
Only a few files changed: --resume and tell Claude exactly which files changed (targeted re-analysis).
Much changed: start a NEW session and inject a structured summary of the valid findings.
To test two designs: use fork_session from the shared baseline.
taskStatements.examTip: Resuming with stale tool results causes wrong answers. A fresh session + summary is more reliable than resuming a session full of outdated data.

testObjectives.text: Explain how the agentic loop uses model responses and stop_reason signals to decide whether to continue tool execution or terminate and return a final response.
keyPoints: Your code, not Claude's words, controls the loop
Append the WHOLE assistant message (text + tool_use) to history
tool_use -> run tools -> one user message with all tool_results -> call again
Any other stop_reason: handle explicitly; never assume success
Distractors: stop when text appears / after N loops / when Claude says done

testObjectives.text: Decompose complex tasks into dynamically generated subtasks that adapt as new information is discovered, rather than executing a fixed sequence regardless of intermediate findings.
keyPoints: Discovery step first (map structure, list sources)
Generate subtasks from findings
Re-plan after each result: add, drop, reorder
Stop when goal criteria are met, not when a fixed list ends
'open-ended', 'unknown codebase' -> dynamic; 'predictable', 'same steps every time' -> chaining

testObjectives.text: Design orchestration-layer safeguards ensuring every agent session ends with a completed resolution or human escalation, regardless of how the agentic loop terminates.
keyPoints: Loop can end via end_turn, max_tokens, refusal, iteration cap, timeout, exception
Wrap loop in an orchestrator with try/finally
Define success in code (resolution_status == 'resolved')
If not resolved on exit -> automatic escalation with structured handoff package
Log the exit reason; no session ends silently

testObjectives.text: Design structured handoff packages that preserve accumulated context, findings, and authorization state when transferring control between agent steps or to a human operator.
keyPoints: Receiver has no transcript
Fields: case/customer ID, authorization state, findings, actions taken, root cause/blocker, recommended action
Authorization state = what is already verified/approved so the receiver does not repeat checks or exceed limits

testObjectives.text: Apply session resumption techniques - including targeted re-analysis of changed files and context injection - to restore agent state accurately without repeating prior work.
keyPoints: Get changed files (git diff --name-only)
Resume named session or start new if stale
Inject: 'Files A, B changed. Re-analyze only these. Prior findings: ...'

testObjectives.text: Apply PreToolUse and PostToolUse hook patterns to enforce business rules and policy constraints not delegated to model discretion.
keyPoints: PreToolUse checks the call and can deny it
PostToolUse changes the result after the tool runs
Rules that must not depend on Claude's judgment go in hooks

traps.wrong: Stop the loop when Claude's reply contains text
traps.why: Claude can return text and a tool call in the same reply

traps.wrong: Use max_iterations = 5 as the main stop condition
traps.right: Use stop_reason; keep a cap only as a safety net
traps.why: A cap cuts off valid work

traps.wrong: Add 'ALWAYS verify identity first' in CAPS to the prompt
traps.why: Prompts have a non-zero failure rate

traps.right: Pass context explicitly in the Task prompt

traps.wrong: Let subagents call each other directly
traps.right: Route all messages through the coordinator

traps.wrong: Fix missing report topics in the search agent
traps.why: The coordinator set the scope too narrow

traps.wrong: Review 14 files in one big pass

traps.right: New session + summary when results are stale

traps.why: Humans often have no transcript access

domains.title: Tool Design & MCP Integration
domains.summary: How you describe tools so Claude picks the right one, return errors so agents can recover, distribute tools across agents, configure MCP servers, and use Claude Code's built-in tools.

taskStatements.title: Tool Interface Design
taskStatements.oneLine: The tool description is the main selection signal.
concept: Claude chooses a tool mainly from its description. Short or vague descriptions cause misrouting. Overlapping descriptions (analyze_content vs analyze_document) confuse Claude.

A good description has: what the tool does and returns; input format (e.g. 'order ID, format ORD-12345'); example queries; edge cases and boundaries (when NOT to use it and which tool to use instead).
Also check the system prompt: keyword-based instructions ('for any order question, check the order') can create unintended tool associations.
steps: Read the descriptions of the confused tools side by side.
Expand each: purpose, inputs, outputs, examples, and 'use X instead when...'.
If tools still overlap, RENAME them or SPLIT a generic tool into purpose-specific tools (analyze_document -> extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim_against_source).
Remove system-prompt keywords that push Claude to the wrong tool.
Test again with the failing queries.
taskStatements.examTip: The FIRST fix for wrong tool selection is better tool descriptions (low effort, high impact). Few-shot examples, a routing classifier, or merging tools are heavier options that come later.

taskStatements.title: Structured Error Responses
concept: In MCP a failed tool result sets the isError flag. A generic 'Operation failed' gives Claude no way to recover - return structured error data.
Access failure vs valid empty result: 'database timed out' is an ERROR. 'No orders found for this customer' is a SUCCESSFUL result with zero items. Never mix them up.

table.title: Error categories
rows: Retry with backoff, locally in the subagent
Correct the input, then call again
Do not retry. Explain to customer in friendly words. Escalate if needed
Do not retry. Escalate or ask for access

steps: Set isError: true.
Add errorCategory (transient / validation / business / permission).
Add isRetryable (true / false).
Add a clear human-readable description (for business errors, a customer-friendly explanation).
In the subagent: retry transient errors locally.
If still unresolved: return to coordinator with the category, what was attempted, and any partial results.
taskStatements.examTip: Agent keeps retrying a policy violation -> the error lacks isRetryable:false and a business category. Agent tells user 'no orders' when DB was down -> tool did not separate access failure from empty result.

taskStatements.title: Tool Distribution and Tool Choice
taskStatements.oneLine: 4-5 tools per agent. tool_choice: auto / any / forced.
concept: Too many tools reduce selection accuracy: an agent with 18 tools makes more wrong choices than one with 4-5 focused tools. Tools outside an agent's role get misused.

Give each agent ONLY the tools for its role (least privilege). Allow a scoped cross-role tool when high-frequency and simple (limited verify_fact for the synthesis agent). Replace generic tools with constrained ones (fetch_url -> load_document).

table.title: tool_choice options
rows: Claude may call a tool or reply with text
Claude MUST call a tool but chooses which
Structured output with several possible schemas (document type unknown)
A specific step must run first (extract_metadata before enrichment)

steps: Guarantee structured output from unknown documents: define one extraction tool per document type.
Set tool_choice: any so Claude must call one of them.
Claude picks the matching schema; you always get a tool_use block, never plain text.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Claude sometimes returns text instead of calling the tool' -> change auto to any (or force the tool). 'Must run tool X first' -> forced {type:tool,name:X}.

taskStatements.title: MCP Server Integration
concept: MCP connects Claude to external systems. Use resources to give Claude a catalog up front, reducing exploratory tool calls.
Tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time and are available at the same time.

Build vs reuse: standard integration (Jira, GitHub, Slack) -> existing community MCP server. Team-specific workflow -> custom MCP server. Claude prefers built-in Grep over your MCP search tool -> improve the MCP tool description.

table.title: MCP primitives
rows: Issue summaries, doc hierarchy, DB schema

steps: Create .mcp.json in the project root.
Add the server entry (command, args).
Put secrets as env variables: "GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITHUB_TOKEN}". Never commit the real token.
Commit .mcp.json. Each developer sets the variable locally.
Personal/experimental servers: local scope (default, this project) or user scope (all projects). Both stored in ~/.claude.json, not shared.
Verify with /mcp or claude mcp list.
taskStatements.examTip: 'New team member does not get the MCP server' -> it is in ~/.claude.json (user level); move to project .mcp.json. 'Token in the repo' -> ${ENV_VAR} expansion.

taskStatements.title: Built-in Tools
taskStatements.oneLine: Grep = content. Glob = file names. Edit = unique match. Read + Write = fallback.
concept: Each built-in tool has one job. Do not confuse Grep (contents) with Glob (paths).

table.title: Built-in tools
rows: Read the full content of a file
Open a file found by Grep
Create or fully overwrite a file
Targeted change by matching a UNIQUE text string

steps: Understand an unfamiliar codebase: Glob to see structure.
Grep to find entry points (main(, route definitions).
Read those files; follow imports.
Trace a function through wrappers: find the exported name, then Grep for it across the codebase.
Build understanding incrementally. Do NOT read every file up front.
When Edit fails (text not unique): add surrounding lines to make it unique, or fallback: Read the whole file, change it, Write the whole file.
taskStatements.examTip: Content search = Grep. File-name pattern = Glob. Edit needs a unique anchor.

testObjectives.text: Configure MCP servers and project settings at the correct scope - project-level for shared team tooling and user-level for personal or experimental configurations.
keyPoints: Local (default): ~/.claude.json under this project, not shared
Project: .mcp.json in repo, shared via git
User: ~/.claude.json, all your projects, not shared
Precedence if same name: local > project > user (fields not merged)
Settings files: managed > .claude/settings.local.json (you, this project) > .claude/settings.json (team, git) > ~/.claude/settings.json (you, all projects)
Audience words: 'team', 'new hires' -> project; 'experimental', 'personal' -> local/user

testObjectives.text: Configure the tool_choice parameter to guarantee tool invocation when structured output is required, and sequence multi-tool workflows so prerequisite data is obtained before dependent tools are called.
keyPoints: Turn 1: force the prerequisite tool (tool_choice type tool + name)
Turn 2+: set back to auto (or any)
Add a code gate: reject the dependent call without valid prerequisite data
Forcing a tool on every turn can create an endless loop
With extended thinking only auto and none are supported
Distractor: 'add always call extract first to the prompt'

testObjectives.text: Improve tool selection reliability by expanding tool descriptions with use-case examples, input format specifications, and explicit disambiguation guidance for semantically similar tools.
keyPoints: Three parts: use-case examples, input format, disambiguation
Weak: 'search_orders: Searches orders.' Strong: purpose + returns + examples + inputs + 'use X instead when...'
Still the first and best fix vs routing classifier / fine-tuning / merging tools

testObjectives.text: Integrate MCP servers into Claude Code and agent applications by selecting the correct server scope, configuring authentication via environment variable expansion, and verifying tool discovery.
keyPoints: claude mcp add --transport http github --scope project <url>
"Authorization": "Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}"; defaults allowed: ${API_URL:-https://api.example.com}
Verify with /mcp (Connected / Needs authentication / Failed) or claude mcp list
Unset variable shows a warning in /mcp

testObjectives.text: Implement MCP tool error handling that surfaces structured, type-specific error information to the agent - including recoverability status and suggested next actions - rather than generic failure messages.
keyPoints: Example: {isError:true, errorCategory:'validation', isRetryable:true, message:'date must be YYYY-MM-DD', suggestedAction:'Reformat date and retry'}

testObjectives.text: Apply systematic codebase exploration strategies using Grep, Glob, and Read tools that build incremental understanding while managing context window constraints.
keyPoints: Order: Glob (map) -> Grep (locate) -> Read (targeted, offset/limit)
Use file-list output from Grep first
Record findings in a scratchpad
Delegate very wide searches to an Explore subagent, keep only its summary
Distractors: read every file first; Grep for *.test.ts (that is Glob); Glob for a function name (that is Grep)

traps.wrong: Add a routing classifier to fix tool confusion
traps.why: Descriptions are the main selection signal; lowest effort

traps.right: Return errorCategory, isRetryable, and a message
traps.why: The agent needs data to recover

traps.wrong: Return an empty list when the service times out
traps.why: Empty result is not an access failure

traps.wrong: Give every agent all 18 tools for flexibility
Keep tool_choice auto and add 'always use the tool' to the prompt
traps.right: Use any or a forced tool

traps.wrong: Put the team MCP server in ~/.claude.json

traps.why: Secrets must not enter version control

traps.wrong: Use Glob to find where a function is called
Build a custom MCP server for Jira
traps.why: Build custom only for team-specific workflows
